_comment: One or two short coaching cues per Studio LFT exercise, keyed by normalized name (lowercase; '.' and '-' become spaces). 'cues' are what a coach says out loud and render in quote marks; 'technical' are the deeper form and progression notes a coach scans before the set, and render in their own block. Rendered under each exercise on the day card. Entries whose exercise also appears in exercise-library.json reuse that entry's cues so the two apps stay consistent.

snatch grip elevated deadlift: Wide grip and the elevation both lengthen the range — the back must stay set throughout
Reduce the deficit before reducing the grip width
spanish split squat: The band behind the knee pulls it back, so drive forward against it
split squat hold + oh ball slam: Hold the bottom of the split squat while you slam — rising up between reps is the cheat
Switch legs every 10 slams and keep the hold depth honest
split squat jumps: Load both legs evenly before the jump and land on the same side you started
Land soft; when the landings get loud, end the set
squat jump: Land in the same stance you left from, soft and quiet
Quality of landing ends the set, not the rep count
squat jump w/ stick: Stick the landing in a quarter squat and hold it before the next rep
The hold is the progression, not the height
standing band hamstring curl: Hips stay still and extended; swinging the thigh forward makes it a hip flexor drill
Pause at full flexion before adding band tension
standing clam shell: Foot on the upright, open from the hip, stay tall and don't lean away
Pause at the open position rather than rushing reps
standing pec stretch: Elbow slightly above the shoulder, then press the chest forward, not the arm back
Hold longer rather than pushing harder
sumo med ball zercher good morning: Wide stance, ball in the elbows, hinge back with a flat back
The ball position pulls the chest down — keep it light and slow
t spine rotation: The turn comes from the mid-back with the hips staying still
Hold the end range for two breaths rather than swinging through
tuck jump: Knees come to the chest, the chest doesn't drop to the knees
Reset fully between reps; continuous tuck jumps degrade fast
v in and out’s: Legs and chest move together and the low back stays down
Bend the knees to shorten the lever before reducing reps
wall support sl standing clam: Hips stay square to the wall; opening the whole body is the easy version
Pause at the open position before adding a band
wall support standing clam: Hips stay square to the wall; opening the whole body is the easy version
Pause at the open position before adding a band
wide grip pull up assisted as needed: Shoulder blades set before the arms pull; full extension at the bottom
Use only as much assistance as it takes to keep the full range
z press: Legs straight and sat tall — any lean back means the position has gone
Build the seated position first; load comes a long way after
½ kneeling high angle face pull: Pull to eyebrow height with the elbows above the wrists, ribs down
Lighter band through the full range beats a heavy band and a short pull
½ kneeling pallof press: Inside knee down, perpendicular to the rack; press straight out without turning
Step further from the anchor for more rotational demand
